question.problem: Let $A(1,2,3,-1)$, $B(0,1,2,0)$, and $C(1,1,3,0).$ Find the cosine of the angle $∠BAC.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $v=\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $w=\overset{\to }{AC}.$ Then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =b-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}w & =c-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Let $\theta =m∠BAC$ be the angle between the vectors $v$ and $w.$ Then, we can find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{v\cdot w}{‖v‖\,‖w‖} \\  & =\frac{{v}_{1}{w}_{1}+{v}_{2}{w}_{2}+{v}_{3}{w}_{3}+{v}_{4}{w}_{4}}{\sqrt{{v}_{1}^{2}+{v}_{2}^{2}+{v}_{3}^{2}+{v}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{w}_{1}^{2}+{w}_{2}^{2}+{w}_{3}^{2}+{w}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 0+1\cdot 1}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{4}\cdot \sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}
$$
